method: Read-only review of assigned artifacts and bounded primary-source rechecks. No downloads, code execution, media reads, or implementation validation.

sources.title: FFmpeg downloads and release branches
sources.version_or_commit: FFmpeg 9.0.2 stable release, announced 2026-09-18; release page also describes 8.1.3 and 8.0.3 branches
sources.locator: Releases section; description of point releases and development branch
sources.observed_operation: Read official release status and branch policy.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Point releases add selected important fixes; the development branch is where developers actively work and receives changes faster. Do not treat docs on a moving branch as proof of a particular binary's enabled codecs.
sources.applicability: Pin one FFmpeg release/build and qualify upgrades against the museum corpus.

sources.title: ffprobe documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current moving upstream documentation read 2026-10-12; use with FFmpeg 9.0.2 release reference S01, but documentation URL itself is not version-pinned
sources.locator: -output_format json; -show_format; -show_streams; -show_error; -show_versions; -show_optional_fields
sources.observed_operation: Read machine-readable probing, container/stream report sections, error and version reporting.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: JSON supports structured output. The default optional-field behavior is auto; JSON/XML omit invalid or non-applicable values. Missing fields therefore do not mean numeric zero.
sources.applicability: Support provenance-rich metadata extraction and honest unknown-duration states; exact output depends on pinned binary/build.

sources.title: FFmpeg stream selection
sources.version_or_commit: Current moving upstream manual; FFmpeg release baseline S01
sources.locator: Section 4.1.1 Automatic stream selection and 4.1.2 Manual stream selection
sources.observed_operation: Read the selection rules for output mapping.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Without -map, audio selection favors the stream with the most channels; equal candidates choose the lowest stream index. Explicit mapping selects only mapped streams, subject to filtergraph outputs.
sources.applicability: Use explicit track indexes for per-speaker review and derivatives.

sources.title: FFmpeg audio filters
sources.version_or_commit: Current moving upstream manual; FFmpeg release baseline S01
sources.locator: Filter sections channelsplit, channelmap and pan
sources.observed_operation: Read channel split/remap options and examples.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: channelsplit defaults input channel_layout to stereo; requesting channels absent from the selected layout errors. pan remapping is lossless only with zero/one gains and one input per output. Mixing is a different operation.
sources.applicability: Never infer speaker labels or downmix; confirm layout/index and retain any split output only as a derivative.

sources.title: FFmpeg FATE ffprobe tests
sources.version_or_commit: FFmpeg tag n9.0.2
sources.locator: FFPROBE_COMMAND and FFPROBE_OUTPUT_MODES_TESTS definitions
sources.observed_operation: Read upstream regression-test definitions; tests generate a known NUT fixture and test compact, CSV, default, flat, INI, JSON and XML output, with optional XML schema validation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The suite requires selected configured components and test data; source presence does not mean this stage ran those tests or that a custom package is equivalent.
sources.applicability: Use as evidence for versioned structured-output test coverage and mirror output/schema tests in the proposal.

sources.title: Symphonia crate support and feature table
sources.version_or_commit: Crate 0.6.1
sources.locator: Support tables: Formats, Codecs, Metadata, Warnings
sources.observed_operation: Read feature/default table for the released crate.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Only WAV, OGG, MKV, FLAC, PCM, ADPCM and listed metadata support are enabled by default; AIFF, CAF, ISO/MP4, AAC, ALAC, MP3/MP1/MP2 are optional features. Opus is not listed as native support; the separate libopus adapter is S07A.
sources.applicability: The Cargo feature set is part of the promised format/preview support and must be pinned/tested.

sources.title: Symphonia getting-started caller
sources.version_or_commit: Symphonia tag v0.6.1; release commit short hash ee35874 is recorded on S08
sources.locator: Probe/decode example: optional Hint extension; default audio track selection; decoder creation; packet loop
sources.observed_operation: Read upstream caller code.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The example uses .expect for opening/probing/decoder creation and skips IO/decode errors in its pedagogical loop; do not copy its panic/error policy into an intake app. It selects a default audio track, not a museum-assigned speaker track.
sources.applicability: Evidence for integration steps and explicit need for production error taxonomy and track selection.

sources.title: Symphonia libopus adapter
sources.version_or_commit: Adapter 0.3.0; docs specify compatibility with Symphonia 0.6
sources.locator: Crate description, usage and Symphonia compatibility
sources.observed_operation: Read third-party adapter documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The adapter supplies libopus to a custom CodecRegistry; default features bundle libopus unless disabled. This is separate dependency/linking/bundling work.
sources.applicability: Opus support is possible with added integration but is not a claim about native Symphonia 0.6.1 support.

sources.title: Symphonia 0.6.1 release notes
sources.version_or_commit: Release tag v0.6.1; commit ee35874; page shows release day Aug 13 but not year in the retrieved text
sources.locator: New Features and Bug Fixes & Improvements
sources.observed_operation: Read release/change history.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Release describes fixes for certain MP3 silent sections, Xing/Info and VBRI CRC tags, mono MP1, large attachments/metadata loading and malformed-input memory/panic hardening. These are evidence of known corrected edges, not complete support guarantees.
sources.applicability: Build corpus cases around release fixes and review subsequent upgrades.

sources.title: Symphonia regression-pack discussion
sources.version_or_commit: Discussion opened 2025-01-07; maintainer reply 2025-01-15
sources.locator: Maintainer response on personal-library testing, differing duration calculations, reproducibility and possible known-good metadata/audio fixtures
sources.observed_operation: Read project-owner discussion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Maintainer notes FFmpeg may produce nonzero-start PTS in some MP4s and MediaInfo may calculate duration differently; private media testing was not reproducible due to copyright/size. Discussion is not a formal support guarantee.
sources.applicability: Preserve raw duration provenance and build a rights-cleared, reproducible fixture suite.

sources.title: GstDiscoverer API
sources.version_or_commit: Current moving GStreamer documentation; API page includes per-API Since annotations
sources.locator: GstDiscoverer blocking/non-blocking API; get_duration; GstDiscovererResult enum
sources.observed_operation: Read upstream discovery API docs.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Duration is returned in nanoseconds; results distinguish OK, invalid URI, error, timeout, busy and missing plugins. Asynchronous mode requires a running GMainLoop/GMainContext.
sources.applicability: Possible discovery/preview backend where plugin/runtime packaging is supportable; surface result distinctions.

sources.title: GStreamer missing-plugin design
sources.version_or_commit: Current upstream design document; API notes state core/base-utils >= 0.10.12
sources.locator: Missing URI handler/typefind/demuxer/decoder sections; application-level policy; error reporting
sources.observed_operation: Read plugin absence and diagnostics behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Applications receive missing-plugin messages; the API does not enforce installation policy. Missing demuxer and decoder are not distinguished at one application message layer; partial plugin availability can permit partial playback.
sources.applicability: Report exact readable/preview/plugin states; never auto-install or equate missing decoder with unreadable original.

sources.title: DROID repository and README
sources.version_or_commit: Current develop branch read 2026-10-12; no commit SHA captured
sources.locator: General information, identification and signature-file CLI sections
sources.observed_operation: Read primary tool documentation and examples.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: DROID uses versioned PRONOM-derived internal signatures and can also identify by extension; it exports reports including CSV and allows showing/switching signature files. Signatures can update, so record the actual database versions; latest version is not established here.
sources.applicability: Optional batch format identifier; store method/PUID/signature versions, but do not use as evidence of decodability.

sources.title: The National Archives DROID/PRONOM role guidance
sources.version_or_commit: Current official guidance read 2026-10-12; revision not displayed
sources.locator: DROID identification description and PRONOM signatures coverage paragraph
sources.observed_operation: Read official operator guidance.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Internal signatures are more accurate than extensions when present, but the page says only around 70% of PRONOM entries have signatures. Extension-only or unidentified results remain possible.
sources.applicability: Do not let absent PUID or a tentative/extension match decide unreadability or admission.

sources.title: RFC 8493 BagIt v1.0
sources.version_or_commit: RFC 8493, BagIt File Packaging Format v1.0, October 2018; Informational
sources.locator: Sections 1–2, especially 2.1.3 payload manifest and 2.4 checksum algorithms
sources.observed_operation: Read package directory and payload checksum requirements.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A bag has tag files and a data payload; manifest lines contain checksum plus relative path. BagIt provides transfer integrity but RFC says it is not designed to secure against active attacks.
sources.applicability: Portable handoff with original files plus metadata tags/checksums; catalog semantics, rights and authenticity still need separate design.

sources.title: SQLite transaction documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite docs read 2026-10-12; release/API version not captured
sources.locator: Transactions; read versus write transactions; DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE
sources.observed_operation: Read transaction semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Many concurrent readers are allowed but only one writer. DEFERRED is the default and can fail on write upgrade with SQLITE_BUSY; IMMEDIATE may also return SQLITE_BUSY.
sources.applicability: If selected, serialize checkpoint writes and test recovery/busy handling.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite docs read 2026-10-12; release/API version not captured
sources.locator: Sections 1 and 2: atomic commit overview and hardware assumptions
sources.observed_operation: Read guarantees and stated conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A committed transaction appears all-or-none across interruption; the described mechanism applies only to rollback-journal mode, and WAL uses a different mechanism. Durability depends on storage/VFS/hardware assumptions; no multi-file package-and-database transaction is implied.
sources.applicability: Use record-sized transactions, avoid claiming atomicity across media copy and database state, and fault-test the actual environment.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Recommendation
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation, WCAG 2.2, 12 December 2024
sources.locator: Success Criterion 2.1.1 Keyboard; Success Criterion 4.1.3 Status Messages
sources.observed_operation: Read the normative standard.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: 2.1.1 requires functionality to work from keyboard subject to its path-dependent-input exception. 4.1.3 applies to content implemented using markup languages; it requires status messages to be programmatically determinable without focus. WCAG is for web content and does not itself specify a native widget API.
sources.applicability: Set user-flow acceptance tests; for native UI, verify platform accessibility semantics and screen-reader behavior separately.

sources.title: Library of Congress sound curator guidance
sources.version_or_commit: Current LoC reference page; revision not captured
sources.locator: Table 2: sound preferences for mono/stereo oral histories; accompanying notes
sources.observed_operation: Read the preservation-format context.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The page lists linear PCM WAVE/BWF and AIFF as preferred for mono/stereo while MP3/AAC variants can be acceptable; it presents LoC preference, not a rule that other donor originals must be rejected.
sources.applicability: Use to inform preservation metadata/fixture coverage, never to narrow intake without a museum owner policy.

sources.title: FFmpeg license and legal considerations
sources.version_or_commit: Current FFmpeg licensing page read 2026-10-12; applicable terms depend on exact source/build/dependencies
sources.locator: FFmpeg License; LGPL compliance checklist; --enable-gpl and --enable-nonfree conditions
sources.observed_operation: Read upstream packaging/licensing notes.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Optional GPL components can change FFmpeg licensing; --enable-nonfree produces an unredistributable binary per upstream page. This is not a legal determination for any proposed package.
sources.applicability: Owner must review the exact binary/configuration and distribution model before bundling.

sources.title: ffprobe documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current moving upstream documentation; no tagged release is identified on the page. The investigator pairs it with FFmpeg 9.0.2, but the documentation URL itself is unpinned.
sources.locator: Description; -show_error, -show_format, -show_streams, -show_versions; -show_optional_fields and JSON writer.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and checked the probe output and optional-field documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: JSON/XML omit invalid or non-applicable fields when optional-field behavior is auto, the documented default. ffprobe returns a positive exit code if input cannot be opened or recognized.
sources.applicability: Supports keeping omitted values unknown and separating probe failure from later preview. Qualify the actual pinned binary.

sources.title: FFmpeg command-line documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current moving manual; no release tag in URL. FFmpeg 9.0.2 is the investigator's separate release baseline.
sources.locator: §4.1.1 Automatic stream selection; §4.1.2 Manual stream selection.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official manual and checked the selection rule.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Without explicit mapping, audio selection favors the stream with the most channels; ties select the lowest stream index. -map restricts output to mapped streams, subject to the documented filtergraph exception.
sources.applicability: Supports explicit stream selection for multi-speaker review; not a guarantee that every build can decode a chosen stream.

sources.title: FFmpeg audio filter documentation
sources.version_or_commit: FFmpeg tag n9.0.2; release-pinned source documentation.
sources.locator: Audio Filters, channelsplit (§ around source lines 4090–4101) and pan (§ around 5722–5783).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the tag-pinned raw source and checked channel layout, absent-channel behavior and pure mapping conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: channelsplit defaults its input layout to stereo, defaults channels to all, and errors when requested channels are absent from that layout. pan is described as pure/lossless mapping only with zero/one gains and one input per output.
sources.applicability: Supports explicit layout/index confirmation and avoiding default downmix or speaker labels. Build inclusion still depends on configured filters.

sources.title: FFmpeg FATE ffprobe tests

sources.locator: FFPROBE_COMMAND; FFPROBE_OUTPUT_MODES_TESTS; FATE_FFPROBE configuration.

sources.applicability: Supports proposing structured-output fixture tests while keeping execution status explicitly false.

sources.title: Symphonia 0.6.1 feature manifest and crate docs

sources.applicability: Supports pinning and testing the exact application feature set. Opus adapter is separate integration, not native default support.

sources.title: RFC 8493 BagIt File Packaging Format
sources.version_or_commit: RFC 8493, BagIt v1.0, October 2018; Informational.
sources.locator: §§2.1.2–2.1.3 payload directory/manifest; §5 Security Considerations.
sources.observed_operation: Read the standard's payload and checksum requirements.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Payload manifest lists each payload file exactly once with checksum and base-relative path; BagIt gives corruption/transfer integrity but is not designed against active attacks.
sources.applicability: Supports self-contained portable handoff and checksum validation; it does not supply catalog or rights semantics.

sources.title: SQLite transaction documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current moving SQLite documentation; no API/runtime version captured.
sources.locator: Read versus write transactions; DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE behavior.
sources.observed_operation: Read the official transaction documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Multiple concurrent readers are allowed, with only one simultaneous write transaction. Write-upgrade conflicts can produce SQLITE_BUSY.
sources.applicability: Supports serial checkpoint writes and explicit busy/recovery tests if SQLite is chosen.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.version_or_commit: Current moving SQLite documentation; article describes rollback-journal behavior; WAL uses a different mechanism.
sources.locator: §§3.7–3.11 commit sequence; stated storage and flush assumptions.
sources.observed_operation: Read the official commit explanation and conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Atomicity depends on database journaling, flushes and storage/VFS/hardware assumptions. It does not imply an atomic transaction across the application database and separately copied package files.
sources.applicability: Supports MI-01 and the draft's own caveat about cross-filesystem/database recovery.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Recommendation
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation, WCAG 2.2, 12 December 2024.
sources.locator: SC 2.1.1 Keyboard; SC 4.1.3 Status Messages.
sources.observed_operation: Read the normative recommendation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Keyboard SC has a path-dependent-input exception. Status Messages says content implemented using markup languages must expose programmatically determinable status without focus.
sources.applicability: Supports user-flow acceptance criteria; a native UI still needs platform accessibility semantics and screen-reader verification.

sources.title: SQLite transaction documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current official documentation; page last updated 2026-02-18; SQLite runtime version not captured.
sources.locator: Sections 2.1–2.2: read/write transactions, DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE, SQLITE_BUSY.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official transaction page and read its transaction and writer-concurrency sections in a read-only browser review.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Multiple simultaneous read transactions are allowed, with only one simultaneous write transaction. A DEFERRED read-to-write upgrade or IMMEDIATE start can return SQLITE_BUSY. This describes database transactions.
sources.applicability: Supports serial database checkpoint writes and explicit busy/recovery handling if SQLite is chosen; it does not certify external package operations.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.version_or_commit: Current official documentation; article describes rollback-journal mode and says WAL uses a different mechanism; SQLite runtime version not captured.
sources.locator: Sections 1–2 and 3.7–3.11: atomic transaction scope, journal mode, storage/flush assumptions.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official atomic-commit explanation and read its scope and hardware-assumption sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The page describes all-or-none changes within a database transaction under stated storage and flush assumptions. Its detailed mechanism is rollback mode; WAL uses another mechanism. It makes no statement that separate application package files participate in a database transaction.
sources.applicability: Supports limiting the proposal’s database atomicity claim; the conclusion that unrelated package filesystem operations are outside that database transaction is an application-boundary inference.
